claims.statement: TalonHost is a long-running host for a single assistant that owns and jointly starts/stops the agent runtime, channel adapters, and an optional cron scheduler in one asyncio event loop.

Talon is an experimental, alpha-status runtime that ships no production security controls (no complete HITL policy, channel admin gates, sandbox isolation, or multi-tenant boundaries), and channel access must be treated as direct access to the operator's agent, credentials, MCP tools, and local host.

The host shuts down gracefully in a fixed order: it cancels all in-flight agent work first, then stops channels in reverse order, then the scheduler, then the agent runtime, and run_until_stopped blocks on a stop event that signal handlers and request_shutdown can set.

A new inbound message replaces an active turn in the same conversation: Talon cancels it, recovers the latest checkpoint where possible, and uses generations to prevent the cancelled turn from delivering stale output; separate conversations can run concurrently.

Inbound channel messages are dispatched by receive_message, which intercepts the /new (reset conversation) and /stop (cancel in-flight run) commands and pending tool-approval replies before replacing or scheduling a normal agent turn.
The /new command starts a fresh conversation thread by cancelling the current run and incrementing a per-conversation reset counter that is appended to the agent thread id.
When more than one channel is attached, a conversation's agent id is namespaced by channel key so identically named conversations on different providers do not collide.

The AgentRuntime protocol (start/stop/invoke) decouples the host from the agent implementation, and Talon provides EchoAgentRuntime (returns request text) and DeepAgentRuntime (a real Deep Agents graph).
The host falls back to the echo runtime when no model is configured, letting operators exercise host lifecycle and channel wiring without provider credentials.

DeepAgentRuntime.start builds the Deep Agents graph via create_deep_agent, and invoke runs it with a per-invocation recursion limit and a thread_id equal to the conversation id, using an in-memory checkpointer by default so turns in a conversation share history.

DeepAgentRuntime tolerates failures: it retries transient provider, parse, context-limit, and transport errors with exponential backoff, and it sends continuation nudges then a force-summary prompt when the graph returns empty text so a reply is always produced.

DeepAgentRuntime executes shell/filesystem work through a LocalShellBackend rooted at DEEPAGENTS_TALON_WORKSPACE (or the current directory) with a scrubbed child environment that drops secrets and env-hijack keys and replaces PATH with a fixed safe path.

Channel adapters implement the ChannelAdapter protocol; the host registers itself as each channel's message handler (and reaction handler when the channel is a ReactionChannelAdapter) so inbound events flow into receive_message/receive_reaction.

The WhatsApp adapter talks to a bundled Node bridge over loopback only, authenticated with a per-process bearer token, and defaults inbound exposure to self while requiring an explicit acknowledgement env value to enable open exposure to arbitrary senders.
WhatsApp media is clamped to a 64 MiB cap that is lower than the cross-channel default limit because the bridge materializes downloads in memory before writing them.
PersistentCronScheduler is a minute-granularity ticker whose loop wakes on either the tick interval or a stop signal, and on each tick it runs jobs the store reports as due.

Before running a due cron job the scheduler claims the next interval via advance_next_run so a job is not double-run, then records the outcome with mark_job_run and delivers non-silent output, suppressing delivery when output begins with the [SILENT] sentinel.

Cron scheduler lifecycle phases emit structured talon_event JSON log records (cron.tick, cron.dispatch, cron.success, cron.failure, cron.delivery, cron.delivery_suppressed, cron.delivery_failure) that complement the persisted last_status and last_error fields.

CronJobStore persists jobs to cron/jobs.json under the assistant state directory, writing atomically through a temp file with fsync and 0600 permissions, namespaced by assistant id and scoped by origin conversation.
Cron schedules are parsed from human text such as 'in 30m' (one-shot) or 'every 15m' (recurring), enforce a one-minute minimum granularity, and recurring jobs may carry an optional repeat cap.

Agent-facing cron tools (create_job, list_jobs, edit_job, remove_job) are exposed to DeepAgentRuntime only when a cron store is supplied and are scoped to the current conversation origin via a context variable, so the agent can only manage jobs belonging to the running conversation.
Because scheduled runs cannot surface interactive approval, a gated tool call under a cron trigger is auto-denied with an explanatory message rather than blocking the run.

On a channel-triggered tool-approval interrupt the host records a pending approval keyed by conversation, prompts the originating conversation, and awaits a decision that only the sender who started the run may give, via text reply or emoji reaction.
DEEPAGENTS_TALON_INTERRUPT_ON_TOOLS lists tool names that are additively merged into the agent's interrupt_on configuration so those tools always require Talon's channel approval flow.

LangSmith tracing is enabled only when LANGSMITH_TRACING is truthy and LANGSMITH_API_KEY is present, and when enabled each channel- or cron-triggered agent run is wrapped in a tracing context carrying assistant id, conversation id, trigger, and message metadata.
Structured talon_event logs are redacted for obvious secrets and PII markers (including conversation_id, message_id, sender_id) before emission.

TalonConfig.from_env selects the assistant namespace from DEEPAGENTS_TALON_ASSISTANT_ID (or AGENT_ASSISTANT_ID), validates it as a safe path segment defaulting to 'default', and reads the model from DEEPAGENTS_TALON_MODEL/AGENT_MODEL.
The per-invocation graph recursion limit defaults to 500 and is tunable via DEEPAGENTS_TALON_RECURSION_LIMIT.

Per-assistant state lives under ~/.deepagents/<assistant_id>/, and ensure_home creates the home plus manifest, agents, cron, channels, and media/inbound subdirectories with restrictive 0700 permissions.

On startup the host prunes completed cron jobs older than DEEPAGENTS_TALON_CRON_RETENTION_DAYS (default 30) and deletes inbound media older than DEEPAGENTS_TALON_INBOUND_MEDIA_RETENTION_HOURS (default 24), while WhatsApp credentials are retained until the operator deletes them.
Conversation persistence is intentionally in-memory and not durable across restarts unless a future backend adds thread persistence.
The DeepAgentRuntime derives its system prompt, skills, and subagents from the materialized assistant directory (AGENTS.md, skills/, agents/) when explicit values are not supplied.
The CLI cleans sensitive retained state before constructing the host and attaches PersistentCronScheduler only when one or more channels exist.
A cancellation that does not finish within 30 seconds blocks that conversation until Talon restarts; a checkpoint-recovery failure instead permits a replacement turn with failure metadata.
Talon converts result Markdown media references to outbound channel attachments only when they resolve inside the configured outbound media root, and reports failed attachments in fallback text.
The shared channel exposure policy defaults to self, supports allowlist and open modes, and requires an explicit acknowledgement value before open mode permits arbitrary senders.
Optional local agent activity logging emits run, model lifecycle, and tool-call events with redacted, bounded tool input/output previews; it does not log hidden chain-of-thought.
